title: Review: Binary Search
context: A teammate's binary search, sent for review. Read it against the problem's constraints before deciding what, if anything, is wrong.

findings.title: (lo + hi) / 2 can overflow on huge arrays, but not here
findings.explanation: In general, lo + hi can pass Integer.MAX_VALUE (about 2.1 billion) and wrap to a negative number. This problem allows at most 10^4 values, so lo + hi stays under 20,000.
findings.consequence: None with these constraints. It would matter only for arrays with more than about a billion elements.
findings.repair: Optional: lo + (hi - lo) / 2 is a habit worth having for code that might see very large arrays.
findings.why_preference: With the stated constraints the sum can't overflow, and every public and hidden test passes. Calling it a bug here would be an unsupported claim.

findings.title: else after a return
findings.explanation: The first branch returns, so the else isn't needed: if (nums[mid] < target) on its own line would behave the same.
findings.repair: Optional: drop the else if your team prefers early returns.
findings.why_preference: Both forms run the same comparisons in the same order. It's about how the code reads.

debrief: No defect: this binary search passes every test, including an empty array and the first and last positions. A good review says so plainly and labels anything else as a preference. Inventing a bug costs the author time and trust.
review_status: Written for practice and machine-checked: the code and the repair were run against every test of the problem.
